readerTitle: Everyone said yes. So why is there no order?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (스낵 제조사와 지역 식료품 체인, 주방 리모델링 업체) + 실제 연구 (Webster & Wind 1972의 구매 센터 개념, CEB 2015 구매 참여자 수)
insight: 기업 고객의 '예'는 한 사람의 대답이 아니다. 거래는 가장 조용한 반대자 한 명에 막힐 수 있으므로, 누가 관여하고 각자 무엇을 확인해야 하는지부터 지도로 그린다.
misconception: 담당자가 마음에 들어 하면 거래는 거의 성사된 것이다. 결정권자 한 명만 설득하면 된다.

sources.text: Webster, F. E. & Wind, Y. (1972). A General Model for Understanding Organizational Buying Behavior. Journal of Marketing, 36(2).
Adamson, B., Dixon, M., Spenner, P. & Toman, N. (2015). The Challenger Customer. Portfolio / CEB.
스낵 제조사와 주방 리모델링 사례는 설명용 가상 사례

factChecks.note: 구매 센터(buying center)의 역할 구분(사용자, 영향력자, 구매자, 결정자, 게이트키퍼)은 Webster & Wind(1972)에서 나온 표준 분류입니다. 원문의 역할 이름과 순서를 게시 전 다시 확인하세요.
"평균 약 5.4명"은 CEB 연구(Adamson 외 2015, The Challenger Customer 및 관련 HBR 기고)에서 자주 인용되는 수치입니다. 조사 연도와 대상(B2B 구매 결정에 공식적으로 관여한 인원)을 원문으로 확인하세요. 확인이 어려우면 카드 문장을 "often five or more people"로 바꿉니다.
콘도 이사회의 배관 공사 승인 요건은 지역과 건물마다 다릅니다. 카드에는 특정 법규가 아니라 '이 건물의 규칙'으로만 적었습니다.

cards.title: Everyone said yes. So why is there no order?
body: A small snack maker pitches its new chips to a 40-store grocery chain. The category buyer tastes them, smiles and says, "I love these. Let me take it upstairs."
Three months later there is still no order. Nobody ever said no. The deal just stopped moving.

image.label: A supplier waiting by a phone while a calendar flips through three months
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 작은 스낵 회사 대표가 과자 봉지 샘플을 들고 전화기 앞에서 기다리고, 뒤 벽 달력이 세 장 넘어가는 모션. 실제 브랜드 로고나 마트 상호는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: The buyer loves it and will "take it upstairs."
body: You're the snack maker. The category buyer is clearly on your side. What do you do next?

options.text: Thank her and follow up every week until she has news
options.feedback: Polite and low effort, but you stay blind. If someone upstairs has a concern, you never hear it and can't answer it.

options.text: Send a bigger launch discount to help her make the case
options.feedback: It may help if price is the blocker. But you're guessing, and you give away margin to solve a problem you haven't seen yet.

options.text: Ask her who else signs off, and what each person needs to see
options.feedback: It takes a slightly awkward conversation. In return, you learn where the deal can stall and can prepare for each person.

cards.title: Three quiet vetoes.
body: When the snack maker finally asked, the picture changed. The buyer was only one of several people involved.
list: **Warehouse manager:** the cases don't fit the chain's standard pallets
**Store operations:** new shelf space means removing a proven seller
cards.callout: None of them said no. Each simply didn't say yes.
cards.softwareNote: In software sales, the user who loves your trial is often blocked later by IT security reviews or procurement contracts nobody mentioned.

cards.title: The buying committee
body: A **buying committee** is the group of people who shape a business purchase. Researchers Frederick Webster and Yoram Wind called it the *buying center* in 1972.

They described roles: users, influencers, gatekeepers who control information, buyers who handle the deal, and deciders. One person can hold several roles. Each brings a different question, and any one of them can slow or stop the purchase.

image.label: A circle of people around one product, each with a different question
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 가운데 과자 상자, 주변에 다섯 인물: "User: Will it sell?", "Influencer: Is it any good?", "Gatekeeper: Do we even hear about it?", "Buyer: What are the terms?", "Decider: Is it worth the shelf?". 인물마다 말풍선. 로고 없음.

cards.title: More people than you think.
body: Research by CEB, published in *The Challenger Customer* (2015), found that about 5.4 people were formally involved in a typical business purchase decision.

More people means more questions to answer. It also means agreement gets harder: a deal moves at the speed of the least convinced person. Sellers who only talk to one friendly contact rarely see the others coming.

cards.title: Small buyers have committees too.
body: A family restaurant buying a new oven may need the chef, the owner and the owner's accountant. A household choosing a renovation may involve two partners and a building manager.
The committee is smaller and less formal, but the pattern is the same. The person who calls you is rarely the only one who decides.

cards.title: Don't map a committee that isn't there.
body: Routine, low-cost purchases are often made by one person. Treating every sale as a committee sale wastes time and can annoy a customer who just wants to buy.
And never go around your main contact. Ask them to help you reach the others. Your contact is also your guide, and losing their trust usually loses the deal.

cards.title: Now it's a kitchen remodel.
body: You run a small renovation firm. Maya called you, loves your design for her condo kitchen, and says her partner will "probably be fine with it." The plan moves the sink, which means new plumbing.
What do you do before sending the final quote?

options.text: Send the quote to Maya and wait
options.feedback: Fast and simple, but her partner and the building may raise questions you could have answered. Quotes like this often sit unsigned.

options.text: Offer a short visit with both partners, and ask about building rules for plumbing work
options.feedback: It costs you an extra hour. It brings out the partner's budget concerns and any board approval early, before they quietly stall the job.

options.text: Add a discount for signing within a week
options.feedback: Urgency can speed one person up. It can't fix a partner who hasn't agreed or a building that hasn't approved the work.

cards.title: A business "yes" is a group decision.
body: Find out who else is involved, what each person needs to see, and help your contact bring them along.
**Try it today:** pick one stalled deal or quote. Write down every person who might need to agree, and the one question each would ask.
